paper.title: Distributed Multi-Agent Bandits Over Erdős-Rényi Random Networks

settings.name_in_paper: Distributed multi-agent multi-armed bandit with heterogeneous rewards over Erdős–Rényi random communication graphs
unmapped: N agents communicate over a time-varying random graph G_t obtained by keeping each edge of a fixed connected base graph G independently with link probability p (Erdős–Rényi); G_t need not be connected
heterogeneous rewards: the same arm's reward distribution differs across agents; regret is measured against the global mean (average over agents) of each arm
reward distribution assumptions (e.g. sub-Gaussian/bounded) not available in the provided source (body sections were \input files not included)
settings.definition_quote: We study the distributed multi-agent multi-armed bandit problem with heterogeneous rewards over random communication graphs. Uniquely, at each time step $t$ agents communicate over a time-varying random graph $\mathcal{G}_t$ generated by applying the Erdős–Rényi model to a fixed connected base graph $\mathcal{G}$ ... where each potential edge in $\mathcal{G}$ is randomly and independently present with the link probability $p$. ... The goal is to minimize the cumulative expected regret relative to the global mean reward of each arm, defined as the average of that arm’s mean rewards across all agents.

algorithms.name: Distributed arm elimination with random gossip (proposed fully distributed algorithm)

symbols.p_link: Erdős–Rényi link probability of each edge of the base graph
symbols.lambda_conn: algebraic connectivity lambda_{N-1}(Lap(G)) of the base graph G

source.quote: We theoretically show that the regret upper bound is of order $\log T$ and is highly interpretable, where $T$ is the time horizon. It includes the optimal centralized regret $\calO\left(\sum_{k: \Delta_k>0} \frac{\log T}{\Delta_k}\right)$ and an additional term $\calO\left(\frac{N^2 \log T}{p \lambda_{N-1}(\operatorname{Lap}(\calG))} + \frac{KN^2 \log T}{p}\right)$

results.notes: Only the abstract was available (theorem sections were \input files not included), so the theorem number, exact conditions, noise assumptions, regret definition (pseudo vs expected) and horizon knowledge could not be verified. Delta_k is the gap w.r.t. global means. A nearly optimal lower bound is mentioned but no expression is given, so it is not recorded.
